questions.stem: The SI (Système International) has how many BASE UNITS?

options.option_text: SEVEN — metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela

questions.explanation: THE SEVEN SI BASE UNITS (rebased in 2019 on physical constants): | Quantity | Unit | Symbol | (1) LENGTH = metre (m); (2) MASS = kilogram (kg); (3) TIME = second (s); (4) ELECTRIC CURRENT = ampere (A); (5) TEMPERATURE = kelvin (K); (6) AMOUNT OF SUBSTANCE = mole (mol); (7) LUMINOUS INTENSITY = candela (cd). MNEMONIC: 'Some Kids Must Sail Around To Canada' (S-K-M-S-A-T-C → s, kg, m, s, A, T→K, cd) or 'MKS A K mol cd'. 2019 REDEFINITION: on 20 May 2019 (World Metrology Day), all 7 SI base units were redefined in terms of 7 PHYSICAL CONSTANTS (fixed exact values): (a) Caesium frequency Δνₛ Cs (second); (b) Speed of light c (metre); (c) Planck constant h (kilogram — replaced the last physical artifact, the Sèvres cylinder!); (d) Elementary charge e (ampere); (e) Boltzmann constant k (kelvin); (f) Avogadro number NA (mole); (g) Luminous efficacy Kcd (candela). KILOGRAM was the LAST base unit tied to a physical artefact (IPK — International Prototype of the Kilogram, a 1889 platinum-iridium cylinder in Sèvres, Paris); now defined by Planck's constant via the Kibble balance. SI also has 2 SUPPLEMENTARY units (dimensionless): RADIAN (plane angle) + STERADIAN (solid angle) — now classified as derived.

questions.stem: The SI unit of FORCE is:

options.option_text: NEWTON (N) = kg·m/s² — force required to accelerate a 1 kg mass by 1 m/s²

questions.explanation: NEWTON (N) — SI UNIT of FORCE, named after SIR ISAAC NEWTON. DEFINITION: 1 N = force needed to accelerate a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s². Dimensional formula: [M L T⁻²]. EXAMPLES: a 100-gram apple weighs ~1 N on Earth (mg = 0.1 × 9.8 ≈ 0.98 N); a 10 kg mass weighs ~98 N; an adult's body weight (70 kg) ≈ 686 N. KEY DERIVED SI UNITS: (1) JOULE (J) = N·m = kg·m²/s² → ENERGY / WORK (James Prescott Joule). (2) WATT (W) = J/s → POWER (James Watt); 1 horsepower ≈ 746 W. (3) PASCAL (Pa) = N/m² → PRESSURE (Blaise Pascal); atmospheric pressure ~101325 Pa = 1.013 bar = 760 mmHg. (4) HERTZ (Hz) = s⁻¹ → FREQUENCY (Heinrich Hertz). (5) COULOMB (C) = A·s → ELECTRIC CHARGE. (6) VOLT (V) = W/A = J/C → ELECTRIC POTENTIAL. (7) OHM (Ω) = V/A → RESISTANCE. (8) FARAD (F) = C/V → CAPACITANCE. (9) TESLA (T) = Wb/m² → MAGNETIC FLUX DENSITY. (10) WEBER (Wb) = V·s → MAGNETIC FLUX. (11) LUMEN (lm), LUX (lx) → LIGHT. (12) BECQUEREL (Bq), GRAY (Gy), SIEVERT (Sv) → RADIOACTIVITY. All named SI derived units are named after SCIENTISTS. Dyne (CGS) = 10⁻⁵ N; pound-force (Imperial) ≈ 4.448 N.

questions.stem: The SI unit of ELECTRIC CURRENT is the AMPERE (A). After the 2019 redefinition, one ampere is defined in terms of:

options.option_text: The FIXED VALUE of the ELEMENTARY CHARGE e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; 1 A = flow of (1/e) elementary charges per second
Mass of copper deposited in electrolysis

questions.explanation: AMPERE (A) — SI UNIT of ELECTRIC CURRENT, named after ANDRÉ-MARIE AMPÈRE. 2019 REDEFINITION (20 May 2019): The ampere is defined by taking the FIXED NUMERICAL VALUE of the ELEMENTARY CHARGE e to be exactly 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (coulomb), where the coulomb = A·s. So 1 AMPERE = flow of 1/(1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹) = ~6.2415 × 10¹⁸ elementary charges per second. OLD (pre-2019) DEFINITION: 'that constant current which, when maintained in two straight parallel conductors of infinite length + negligible cross-section, placed 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre of length between them' (based on Ampere's force law). The old definition tied ampere to μ₀ (permeability of free space, exact by definition = 4π × 10⁻⁷). NEW definition frees μ₀ to be a measured quantity. OHM'S LAW: V = IR. 1 A is a SIGNIFICANT current — lethal through heart can be as low as 50 mA; household mains fuse at 6/16/32 A; 1000 A is industrial welding scale; lightning bolt can carry 30,000 A. MILLIAMPERE (mA) = 10⁻³ A; MICROAMPERE (µA) = 10⁻⁶ A.

questions.stem: The SI unit of PRESSURE is:

options.option_text: PASCAL (Pa) = N/m² — named after BLAISE PASCAL

questions.explanation: PASCAL (Pa) — SI unit of PRESSURE + STRESS. 1 Pa = 1 N/m² = 1 kg·m⁻¹·s⁻². NAMED after BLAISE PASCAL (1623-1662), French mathematician/physicist. PASCAL IS A SMALL UNIT — atmospheric pressure at sea level ≈ 1,01,325 Pa = 101.325 kPa = 1.013 bar. Common pressure multiples: kilopascal (kPa = 10³ Pa), megapascal (MPa = 10⁶ Pa), gigapascal (GPa = 10⁹ Pa — material strengths). OTHER PRESSURE UNITS: (1) BAR = 10⁵ Pa (meteorology + industry); millibar (mb) = 100 Pa = 1 hPa (weather maps). (2) ATMOSPHERE (atm) = 101,325 Pa. (3) TORR = 1/760 atm ≈ 133.3 Pa (vacuum). (4) mmHg = 1 Torr (blood pressure, barometers — normal BP 120/80 mmHg = 16/10.7 kPa). (5) PSI (pound per square inch) ≈ 6,895 Pa (tire pressure, US industry; car tire ~30 psi). BOYLE'S LAW: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ (isothermal). PASCAL'S LAW: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid transmits equally in all directions (hydraulic press, brake). ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE: buoyant force = weight of fluid displaced. At Mt Everest summit (8,848m), atm pressure drops to ~33% of sea-level value — why climbers need oxygen. Mariana Trench bottom (~11 km) pressure ~1,100 atm.

questions.stem: One LIGHT-YEAR is approximately equal to:

options.option_text: 9.461 × 10¹² km ≈ 9.46 TRILLION KILOMETRES (distance light travels in 1 year in vacuum at 3 × 10⁸ m/s)

questions.explanation: LIGHT-YEAR (ly) — DISTANCE (not time!) that light travels in one Julian year in vacuum. CALCULATION: speed of light c = 299,792,458 m/s ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s; seconds in a year = 365.25 × 24 × 3600 = 31,557,600 s; distance = c × t ≈ 9.461 × 10¹⁵ m = 9,461,000,000,000 km ≈ 9.46 TRILLION km ≈ 5.88 trillion miles. EXAMPLES: (a) Sun is ~8.3 LIGHT-MINUTES from Earth (not years). (b) PROXIMA CENTAURI (nearest star to the Sun) is 4.24 ly. (c) MILKY WAY galaxy diameter ~100,000 ly. (d) ANDROMEDA GALAXY (M31) ~2.5 million ly. (e) Observable universe diameter ~93 BILLION ly. OTHER ASTRONOMICAL DISTANCES: (1) ASTRONOMICAL UNIT (AU) = mean Earth-Sun distance = 149,597,870,700 m ≈ 150 million km. 1 ly ≈ 63,241 AU. (2) PARSEC (pc) = 3.26 ly ≈ 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m — distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond; used in professional astronomy. 1 kiloparsec (kpc), 1 megaparsec (Mpc). (3) LIGHT-YEAR vs CENTURY in popular media: confusingly used 'I'll wait a light-year' is wrong — light-year is distance. HUBBLE CONSTANT: ~70 km/s/Mpc — measures rate of universe's expansion. REDSHIFT is how distant galaxies are measured.

questions.stem: HORSEPOWER (1 HP, the unit used for engines) equals approximately:

options.option_text: 746 W (metric HP = 735.5 W; imperial/mechanical HP = 745.7 W)

questions.explanation: HORSEPOWER (HP) — originally defined by JAMES WATT in the 1780s as a way to market his improved steam engines to replace horses. He estimated a pit pony could lift 22,000 foot-pounds/min; multiplied by 1.5 to be safe → 33,000 foot-pounds/min = 550 foot-pounds/sec = 746 W (mechanical HP). VARIANTS: (1) MECHANICAL HP (imperial) = 745.70 W — US + UK engine ratings; (2) METRIC HP (PS / CV / cheval vapeur) = 735.5 W — continental Europe, India, Japan; (3) Electrical HP = 746 W exactly (used for electric motor ratings). DIFFERENCE: manufacturer spec sheets: a car rated 100 PS (metric) = 98.6 HP (mechanical); significant for marketing. EXAMPLES: (a) Peak human sprint ~1.2 HP briefly; sustained cycling ~0.1 HP. (b) Honda Activa ~8 HP; Maruti Alto ~67 HP; Toyota Fortuner ~200 HP; F1 car ~1000 HP. (c) Boeing 777 engine ~100,000 HP each. (d) 1 HP air-conditioner = 1 TON cooling in loose Indian usage (technically 1 ton refrigeration = 3.517 kW = 4.71 HP — i.e., '1 Ton AC' ≈ 3.5 kW, but 'horsepower rating' on inverters uses diff scale). SI UNIT: WATT (W) is the proper SI unit of power; 1 kW = 1000 W. 1 kWh (kilowatt-hour) = energy consumed by 1 kW load for 1 hr = 3.6 MJ — your electricity bill 'unit'.

questions.stem: 0 KELVIN (absolute zero) corresponds to approximately what Celsius temperature?

options.option_text: −273.15 °C — theoretical temperature at which particles have minimum vibrational (zero-point) motion

questions.explanation: ABSOLUTE ZERO: the LOWEST possible temperature, where classical molecular motion CEASES (quantum zero-point energy remains). 0 K = −273.15 °C = −459.67 °F. TEMPERATURE SCALE CONVERSIONS: (1) K = °C + 273.15. (2) °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9. (3) °F = °C × 9/5 + 32. KEY POINTS: (a) Water FREEZES at 0°C = 273.15 K = 32°F (at 1 atm). (b) Water BOILS at 100°C = 373.15 K = 212°F (at 1 atm). (c) Human body temp ~37°C = 310.15 K = 98.6°F. (d) Room temp ~25°C = 298.15 K = 77°F. COLDEST NATURAL: Vostok, Antarctica −89.2°C (1983); LOWEST LAB temp: ~38 picokelvin (fraction above 0 K) achieved by Bose-Einstein condensates. DEEP SPACE cosmic microwave background temp ~2.725 K. 3rd LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS: absolute zero is UNATTAINABLE — can approach it asymptotically. ABSOLUTE ZERO was extrapolated by WILLIAM THOMSON (Lord KELVIN) in 1848 — hence K scale. Earlier GAS-LAW data: Charles's Law (V∝T) linearly extrapolated to zero volume at −273°C. RANKINE scale (imperial absolute) rarely used. KELVIN is SI base unit → the only absolute temp in SI; NO 'degree' prefix (write 300 K, not 300°K). Redefined in 2019 via Boltzmann constant k = 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J/K.

questions.stem: The unit PARSEC (pc) used in astronomy equals approximately:

options.option_text: 3.26 LIGHT-YEARS (≈ 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m) — distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond parallax

questions.explanation: PARSEC (pc) — PAR(allax of one) SEC(ond of arc); the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of 1 ARCSECOND. 1 pc = 3.0857 × 10¹⁶ m ≈ 3.262 LIGHT-YEARS ≈ 206,265 AU. USE: professional astronomy — galaxies' distances measured in MEGAPARSECS (Mpc = 10⁶ pc) or KILOPARSECS (kpc = 10³ pc). EXAMPLES: (a) Proxima Centauri ≈ 1.301 pc (≈ 4.24 ly); (b) Milky Way radius ≈ 15-20 kpc; (c) Nearest major galaxy (Andromeda M31) ≈ 780 kpc; (d) Observable universe radius ≈ 14,000 Mpc. HUBBLE CONSTANT: ~70 km/s/Mpc. PARALLAX method: measure a star's apparent shift as Earth moves from one side of its orbit to the other (baseline = 2 AU). Tiny angular shift = 1/distance in pc. Only nearby stars (within ~300 pc) have measurable parallax from Earth; GAIA space telescope (ESA, 2013-launched) has mapped parallax for billions of stars to µarcsec precision — current gold standard for stellar distances. BEYOND parallax: STANDARD CANDLES (Cepheid variables' luminosity-period relation — Henrietta Leavitt, 1912; Type Ia supernovae); REDSHIFT (for distant galaxies, Hubble law). ASTRONOMICAL DISTANCES summary: AU (solar system) → ly or pc (stars) → kpc (galaxy) → Mpc (nearby galaxies) → Gpc (cosmological).

questions.stem: Match the unit with the quantity measured: (1) TESLA (T); (2) WEBER (Wb); (3) HENRY (H); (4) FARAD (F).

options.option_text: Magnetic flux density; Magnetic flux; Inductance; Capacitance

questions.explanation: ELECTROMAGNETIC SI UNITS: (1) TESLA (T) — MAGNETIC FLUX DENSITY (Wb/m² = kg/(A·s²)); named after NIKOLA TESLA. Earth's magnetic field ~25-65 µT; fridge magnet ~5 mT; MRI machine ~1.5-7 T; LHC magnets ~8 T. (2) WEBER (Wb) — MAGNETIC FLUX (= V·s); named after WILHELM EDUARD WEBER. (3) HENRY (H) — INDUCTANCE (V·s/A = Wb/A); named after JOSEPH HENRY, American physicist who discovered self-inductance. (4) FARAD (F) — CAPACITANCE (C/V); named after MICHAEL FARADAY. Typical capacitors in microfarads (µF) or picofarads (pF); 1 F is very large (supercapacitors). OTHER ELECTRIC UNITS: OHM (Ω, Georg Ohm) = resistance; SIEMENS (S) = 1/Ω = conductance; COULOMB (C, Charles-Augustin de Coulomb) = A·s = charge; VOLT (V, Alessandro Volta) = J/C = potential. LUMINOUS UNITS: CANDELA (cd) = luminous intensity (base unit); LUMEN (lm) = luminous flux = cd·sr; LUX (lx) = lm/m² = illuminance. Reading a book needs ~400 lux; direct sunlight ~100,000 lux. RADIATION UNITS: BECQUEREL (Bq, Henri Becquerel) = 1 decay/sec (activity); CURIE (Ci, old unit) = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq; GRAY (Gy, Louis Harold Gray) = J/kg = absorbed dose; SIEVERT (Sv, Rolf Sievert) = J/kg = equivalent dose (biological effect); banana ~0.1 µSv; dental X-ray ~5 µSv; annual natural background ~3 mSv; lethal ~4 Sv.

questions.stem: The SI PREFIX for 10⁻¹² (one trillionth) is:

options.option_text: PICO (p) — as in picofarad (pF), picometre (pm), picosecond (ps)

questions.explanation: SI PREFIX TABLE (magnitude ↑ top, ↓ bottom): | 10²⁴ YOTTA (Y); 10²¹ ZETTA (Z); 10¹⁸ EXA (E); 10¹⁵ PETA (P); 10¹² TERA (T); 10⁹ GIGA (G); 10⁶ MEGA (M); 10³ KILO (k); 10² hecto (h); 10¹ deca (da); 10⁰ BASE UNIT; 10⁻¹ deci (d); 10⁻² centi (c); 10⁻³ MILLI (m); 10⁻⁶ MICRO (µ); 10⁻⁹ NANO (n); 10⁻¹² PICO (p); 10⁻¹⁵ FEMTO (f); 10⁻¹⁸ ATTO (a); 10⁻²¹ ZEPTO (z); 10⁻²⁴ YOCTO (y). 2022 addition (26th CGPM): RONTO (r, 10⁻²⁷), QUECTO (q, 10⁻³⁰), RONNA (R, 10²⁷), QUETTA (Q, 10³⁰). EXAMPLES: (a) PICOSECOND — time for light to travel 0.3 mm; laser pulse timescale. (b) PICOMETRE — atomic scale (H atom radius ~53 pm). (c) PICOFARAD — common capacitor value in electronics. FEMTOSECOND laser = 10⁻¹⁵ s — can photograph electrons in motion (Nobel Physics 2023 to Agostini, Krausz, L'Huillier). ATTOSECOND — 10⁻¹⁸ s, shorter than an electron's orbital period. NANOSECOND: light travels 30 cm in 1 ns — limits clock speed in CPUs. Human reaction time ~200 ms (200 million ns). 'RONNABYTE' + 'QUETTABYTE' = new large data units.
